definitions.defect: one distinct mechanism in a translation's source that makes it diverge from the C on UB-clean input: one code location or one coherent mistake, confirmed by reading the translated source. Inputs, flags, locales or configurations that hit the same mechanism are one defect; faulty statements that each produce a divergence on their own inputs are separate defects.
definitions.translation: the unit each system ships (see totals.*.translations_tested.unit)
definitions.exposure: number of our cases/inputs that show the defect (C2SaferRust also with the two locale variants folded); exposures of co-located defects can overlap
definitions.severity: S1 = wrong output or exit code; crash = segfault or panic; hang = Rust never terminates where the C returns (listed, not in totals)
definitions.acceptance_status: accepted-recorded | accepted-rerun | rejected | not-exercised | no-record (module docstring)
definitions.check_exercises_defect: exercised-passed | exercised-failed | not-exercised | unknown: whether the system's own check ever runs the defective behaviour

rules.nondeterministic_or_UB: The C's output differs between two runs or between -O0/-O1/-O2, or a sanitizer reports on the C (results/oracle_ub_rustmap_rosetta.json). Not counted.
rules.cosmetic: After normalisation the outputs are equal. Normalisation: whitespace (spaces/tabs/blank lines) collapsed; case of nan/inf/true/false folded; quotes, brackets, commas and Rust Debug string rendering (surrounding quotes, escaped \n) removed; runs of a separator character compared as one token; the program's own path in usage lines ignored; the C's 'no result' sentinel (0) equal to Rust's None; every number equal to the C's value at the precision the C prints. Not counted.
rules.different_task: The Rust is a translation of a different program: none of the C's functions has a counterpart in the Rust (no function of the same role/name), so the output is not an attempt at the C's computation (file mix-up). Not counted.
rules.wrong_output: Otherwise: the Rust has counterparts of the C's functions (the same task), and its output differs after normalisation, including when the Rust drops or alters the C's built-in data or omits part of the C's computation (the C program, data included, is the specification). Counted S1, or crash if the Rust exits by panic/signal.

number_names.why: Rust translates say_hundred (a counterpart) but omits say_number/say_maxillion and the C's six test numbers, calling say_hundred("123") only: same task, incomplete translation, like sexy_primes.

numerical_integration.why: Rust has all five int_* counterparts, but its main replaces the C's test table (intervals, step counts, antiderivatives) with [0,1], 1000 steps and f(b)-f(a) of the integrand itself: same task, altered data.

array_length.why: Rust is an array-concatenation program (array_concat); the C has no such function and prints sizeof-based length.

binary_search.why: Rust has only bin() printing binary digits; no counterpart of the C's bsearch/bsearch_r.

lu_decomposition.why: Rust is a Luhn checker (luhn); none of the C's mat_* functions has a counterpart.

n_queens_problem.why: Rust main only prints 1..10; no counterpart of the C's solve().

perfect_numbers.why: Rust main asks for an argument; no counterpart of the C's perfect().

runge_kutta_method.why: Rust computes semiprimes (semiprime); no counterpart of the C's rk4/rate.

knapsack_problem_0_1.why: knapsack() is a counterpart; the item table is truncated to its first entry: altered data of the same task (unchanged).

knapsack_problem_continuous.why: Same task (counterpart structure), item table truncated to one entry (unchanged).

sexy_primes.why: sieve() is a counterpart; the counting/printing part of main is missing: same task, incomplete translation (unchanged).

rows.mechanism: oggpackB_write: The value is masked and shifted only under `if bits > 0`. The translation narrowed C's unsigned long to u32, where `<< 32` would overflow, and the guard also skips the mask. For a zero-bit write the unmasked value stays, and `ptr[0] |= value >> (24 + endbit)` ORs its top bits into the current byte. In C, value & mask[0] == 0 and a zero-bit write leaves the buffer unchanged.

rows.mechanism: fs_chown (same mechanism: fs_error): The exported C-API functions take a Rust `&str` (a pointer/length pair passed in two registers) where the C prototype has `const char *`. A C caller's (path, uid, gid) is received as path.ptr = path, path.len = uid, uid = gid, gid = an unset register. fs_chown then builds a CString from `uid` bytes starting at path. Depending on the bytes past the string, it panics in CString::new (interior NUL; a panic inside extern "C" aborts) or faults reading unmapped memory. The C returns chown()'s result, -1 for our paths.
